notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found). §1985:VII.1.3.5 lists the logic-error values of a sequential file: 41 (OPEN of a file in the open mode), 42 (CLOSE of a file not in the open mode), 43 (REWRITE not preceded by a successfully executed READ), 44, 46 (a sequential READ with no valid next record after an unsuccessful or at end READ), 47 (READ on a file not open in the input or I-O mode), 48 (WRITE on a file not open in the output or extend mode) and 49 (REWRITE on a file not open in the I-O mode). Seven conform at --std 85, each probed: FileConnector.Open gives 41 (OPEN OUTPUT, INPUT and I-O of an open file); FileConnector.Close and FileRegistry.CloseCell give 42 (never opened, closed twice, after a failed OPEN); SequentialConnector.Rewrite gives 49 through MutationOpenModeGuard (not open, INPUT, OUTPUT, EXTEND) and then 43 when PrevOpWasSuccessfulRead is false (no READ, a second REWRITE, after an at end READ); SequentialReadGuard gives 47 through ReadOpenModeGuard (not open, OUTPUT, EXTEND) and 46 after an unsuccessful READ (after at end, and again after the 46); SequentialConnector.Write gives 48 (not open, INPUT, I-O). 44 conforms for its two 1985 causes: OutsideVaryingBounds refuses a WRITE or REWRITE outside a RECORD IS VARYING range (7 and 2 characters under FROM 3 TO 6: 44, DEPENDING ON item unchanged) and RewriteRecordSequential refuses a REWRITE whose size differs from the record read (44, record unchanged on re-read). What does not conform is a third cause the 1985 list does not have: BindRecordClause stores a Format 3 clause (RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5) in the same FileModel.Varying as Format 2, RecordSizeVaries passes its integers to the connector as the range, and OutsideVaryingBounds then answers 44 at every edition, so at 85 a WRITE of a record shorter than integer-4 or longer than integer-5 is unsuccessful and the record is not stored. That is §2023:13.18.43.4 GR19, which 1985 does not have: 1985 item 44 1) names only "the RECORD IS VARYING clause", and for Format 3 §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14 says "the size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry"; no 1985 rule makes that WRITE unsuccessful, and the row's change record names this difference. The witness shows the USE procedure run with 42 on the second CLOSE.

next.reason: 41, 42, 43, 46, 47, 48 and 49 carry over for sequential files; 46's two 1985 causes fall under 'The preceding READ statement referencing that file connector was unsuccessful' (§2023:9.1.13.7 GR6), since an at-end READ is unsuccessful. The added DELETE FILE, UNLOCK, START and DELETE RECORD cases need statements 1985's sequential module lacks. Status 44 differs: 2023 adds a failure when a record falls outside the range 'allowed by the fixed-or-variable-length format of the RECORD clause when the implementor has specified that variable-length records are produced' (§2023:9.1.13.7 GR4c), driven by 'If the number of bytes in the logical record to be written is less than integer-4 or greater than integer-5' the WRITE/REWRITE is unsuccessful (§2023:13.18.43.4 GR19). 1985 RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5 sets no such check ('the size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry', §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13), so such a 1985 WRITE that succeeded can now fail with 44. The line sequential case d) is new syntax.
